House Extension Costs

The price of a home extension is set by what goes into the ground and what goes on top, far more than by the floor area alone. Two extensions with the same footprint can be priced very differently once the survey shows what is under the lawn and how the new roof meets the old one.

A written quote from us breaks the job into the stages it is built in, so you can see where the money sits:

  • Substructure: excavation, concrete strip footings, the blockwork up to damp proof course and the ground floor slab.
  • Superstructure: the cavity walls, lintels, any steel beams and padstones where the extension opens into the house.
  • Roof: a pitched roof tied into the existing slope, or a flat roof with falls to a gutter.
  • Openings and finish: windows, doors, first and second fix, plastering and making good where the old wall came out.

Items nobody can see until the ground is open, such as an old drain run under the footprint, are listed as provisional sums rather than hidden in the total. That keeps the quote honest about what is known and what is not.

Planning Permission and Permitted Development in Hedge End

Many single storey rear extensions can be built under permitted development, without a full planning application, provided they stay inside set limits. On an attached house the usual depth limit is 3 metres from the original rear wall, 4 metres on a detached house, and the height cannot exceed 4 metres. Larger single storey rear extensions, up to 6 metres attached or 8 metres detached, go through the prior approval process instead, where neighbours are notified. Two storey extensions and most side extensions need planning permission from Eastleigh Borough Council.

Estate houses in Grange Park and Turnpike Way

Grange Park is a 1960s to 1970s estate and Turnpike Way was built in the 1980s and 1990s. Houses from both eras sometimes had permitted development rights removed by a condition when the estates were given planning consent, so a rear extension that would be allowed elsewhere may still need an application here. We check the planning history of the house before drawings are finalised.

Older plots around St John's

Hedge End was known in the late 19th century as the Strawberry Village, and the older plots around St John's still carry houses from before the estates arrived. Gardens here are often long and narrow, which suits a rear extension but brings the boundary close on both sides. Where the new foundations sit within 3 metres of a neighbour's and go deeper, the Party Wall etc. Act 1996 applies and notices go out before digging starts.

Newer homes at Dowd's Farm

Recent schemes such as Dowd's Farm bring a variety of house types, some with planning conditions that affect what can be added. A lawful development certificate confirms the position in writing before you commit to the build.

Materials, Finishes and Specification

An extension should read as part of the house. That starts with the walls and carries through to the roof covering and the windows.

Walls and brick matching

New walls are cavity construction: a facing brick outer leaf, an insulated cavity, and a blockwork inner leaf tied with stainless steel wall ties. The facing brick is matched to the house for size, colour and texture, and the bond is carried round so the join to the old wall does not show. The damp proof course sits at least 150mm above finished ground level and lines up with the existing one.

Openings, lintels and steel

Every window and door gets a lintel sized for the span, with a cavity tray and weep vents above to carry water out of the wall. Where the extension opens into the existing house, a steel beam on padstones takes the load of the wall above. The beam size comes from a structural engineer's calculations, and building control inspects it before it is covered.

Roof and finish

Pitched roofs are tiled to match the house where the pitch allows it. Flat roofs are built as a warm deck, with the insulation above the joists and falls to a gutter so water never sits on the surface.

Cost Drivers and Budget Risks

Three things move an extension budget more than anything else, and all three are decided early.

  1. The ground. Trees near the footprint, soft ground or an existing drain under the extension can mean deeper footings or a diverted run. The survey looks for these before the price is fixed.
  2. The opening into the house. Removing a load-bearing rear wall needs a steel beam, temporary propping and building control sign-off. A wider opening means a larger beam.
  3. Changes after work starts. Moving a window once the walls are up costs more than moving it on the drawing. Every change is priced in writing before it goes ahead.

If you are looking for a home extension near you in Hedge End, these three are the points worth settling at the survey, before a price is agreed.

Design and Build Process

The build follows the same sequence on every single storey extension, and each stage is signed off before the next begins:

  1. Survey and drawings. Measured survey, your drawings or a designer's, and structural calculations where steel is involved.
  2. Approvals. Planning or permitted development confirmed, Building Regulations submitted, and party wall notices served where needed. The work is built to The Building Regulations 2010.
  3. Groundworks. Excavation, footings inspected by building control, then blockwork to damp proof course and the slab.
  4. Shell. Cavity walls, lintels and steel, then the roof. The house stays sealed until the extension is weathertight.
  5. Break-through and finish. The existing wall is opened only once the new room is dry, followed by first fix, plaster and second fix.
  6. Completion. Final building control inspection and the completion certificate.

Keeping the old wall in place until the shell is closed means the house stays warm and secure for most of the build.

The Quick Answer

  • The old wall stays up until the new shell is closed, so the house stays sealed through the outside work.
  • Dusty work inside is grouped into as few days as the job allows, with rooms sealed off first.
  • Unknowns in older Hedge End houses are priced as provisional sums, not hidden in the total.
  • Building control inspects each stage, and you receive the completion certificate at handover.
  • New builds carry a 10-year warranty.

The same team behind our extension builders services Hedge End homeowners use for rear extensions also builds new homes, lofts and structural openings across the town.

Send a Quick Quote Online with the job, the postcode and any drawings, and Pete Bartlett will arrange a visit.

Builders in Hedge End take on everything from a new home to a knocked-through kitchen, and the order of work matters more than the size of the job. Buildings For Life Ltd runs the groundworks, brickwork, structure and joinery with its own family team, so each trade follows the last without a gap.

Building Services Under One Roof

Open up almost any wall in a Hedge End semi and you find the same thing: brick outside, block or brick inside, and a cavity that has been bridged by mortar somewhere along the way. The trades that deal with it rarely stop at their own layer. The bricklayer needs the lintel in, the carpenter needs the wall plate level, and the plasterer needs both finished before the first coat goes on.

That is why we keep the trades in one firm. The same team digs the footings, lays the brick and block, sets the steel, pitches the roof and hangs the doors. When one stage finishes, the next starts the following morning.

  • Groundworks, foundations and drainage
  • Brickwork and natural stone
  • Steel beams, lintels and structural openings
  • Roofs, carpentry and joinery, including kitchens
  • Plastering, making good and finishing

One firm, one programme, one person answerable.

Home Extensions and Conversions

A rear extension looks like a new room. On site it is mostly a hole in the ground for the first stretch: strip footings dug and concreted, blockwork brought up to damp proof course, then the slab. Nothing above ground can start until building control has seen the footings.

Conversions start from the other end. A loft needs new floor joists that sit clear of the old ceiling, a steel or two to carry them, and a staircase that meets the headroom rules. A basement starts with the ground and the water in it. We handle both kinds of job.

Where the new room joins the house, the old wall stays in place until the new shell is closed. You keep a sealed house while the extension goes up outside it.

Design and Build Planning

A cut wall throws dust into every room it can reach, so the order of work decides the disruption more than the size of the job. We plan it in stages so you know which part of the house is affected and when.

Survey and drawings

We measure the house, look at the ground and the access, and work from your drawings or a designer's. Where a load-bearing wall comes out, a structural engineer sizes the steel before the price is fixed.

Approvals and notices

Planning or permitted development is confirmed, Building Regulations are submitted, and party wall notices go to the neighbours where the work is close to a shared wall or boundary.

Staging the work around you

Outside work comes first: footings, walls and roof. Inside work, such as opening a wall or moving a kitchen, is grouped so the dusty days come together and the room you lose is lost once. Dust sheets and sealed doorways go up before any wall is cut.

Handover

Building control makes a final inspection and issues the completion certificate. You get the paperwork along with the keys to the new room.

Renovations and Refurbishments

Older houses in Hedge End were built before most of the estates, when the town was still known as the Strawberry Village, and they rarely match modern drawings. Floors fall, walls lean and lintels turn out to be timber. We expect it and price the unknowns as provisional sums.

A refurbishment usually means opening up rooms, moving or blocking openings, new steel where a wall comes out, and a proper finish afterwards. Kitchens and joinery are fitted by the same team that did the structural work, so the units meet walls that are square because we made them square.

You can stay in the house through most refurbishments. The rooms being worked on are closed off, and the kitchen, if it is part of the job, is the last room out of action.

Building Work for Landlords and Property Owners in Hedge End

An empty house is the simplest place to work: no furniture, no family and no kitchen to keep running. Hedge End has grown faster than any other town in the Borough of Eastleigh over the last twenty years, and plenty of its houses change hands or tenants between those gaps.

Our builder services fit the structural work those gaps allow, from a new rear room to repairs to failed brickwork, and we plan it to fit the time the property is empty. Whether you need builders in Hedge End or loft conversions in Hedge End, the same family team covers the whole town, from Grange Park and Turnpike Way to the newer streets at Dowd's Farm.

New Builds and Structural Work for Hedge End Homes

A new home starts where every extension starts, with the ground. Trial holes show what the footings sit on, and the drainage is set out before a single course of brick goes down. From there it is walls, floors, roof and the long list of fixings that turn a shell into a house.

Structural work on existing homes follows the same discipline. Steel beams sit on padstones, lintels get cavity trays, and new foundations go deep enough for the ground they are in. A builder who started as a bricklayer, as Pete Bartlett did over 40 years ago, checks those details himself because they are the ones you never see again.

New builds carry our 10-year warranty. The walls stay where they are put.

title: Loft Conversions in Hedge End
metaTitle: Loft Conversions in Hedge End | Local Family Run Business
description: Loft conversions in Hedge End: dormer and roof-light lofts built from outside, with new joists, steel, a proper stair and building control sign-off.
summary: Pete Bartlett and the Buildings For Life Ltd team convert lofts across the town, from the structure and dormer to the stairs and fire doors. Call Pete or send photos of your roof to book a survey.
heroAlt: Insulation boards fitted between new roof rafters during a loft build
bodyHtml:
Hedge End is full of family houses that ran out of bedrooms long before the family ran out of reasons to stay, and the roof space above them is usually empty.

At a Glance

  • The roof shape decides the work: a hip roof needs more than a gable to gain headroom.
  • New floor joists and steel carry the room, sized by an engineer before the price is fixed.
  • The roof and dormer are built from outside, so the house below keeps running.
  • Many lofts fall under permitted development, but Building Regulations sign-off is always needed.

The family team behind our new builds services Hedge End homeowners know also converts lofts across the town, from Grange Park semis to the newer estates.

Send a Quick Quote Online with a photo of your roof from the street and one from the loft hatch, and Pete will come and look.

Converting the roof space of a Hedge End family house gives you a bedroom or a study without giving up any of the garden. The awkward parts are the structure, the staircase and the fire route, and Buildings For Life Ltd handles all three with its own team.

Ask Buildings For Life Ltd about Loft Conversions in Hedge End and find out at the survey whether your hip or gable roof gives the headroom a proper room needs.

Quick Quote OnlineCall Now: 07853 945013

Loft Conversion Costs

What the roof decides

On a loft conversion the roof decides the work, not the room. A hip roof on a 1960s to 1970s Grange Park semi needs more work to gain headroom than a straight gable does. A dormer adds walls, a roof and windows. A roof-light conversion adds almost none. Same floor area, different job.

What sits under the floor

The old ceiling joists were never meant to carry a bedroom. Structure comes first. New floor joists go in beside them, often carried on steel beams that bear on the walls below. The engineer's calculations size them. That is fixed cost, whatever the finish.

How the quote is written

Your written quote breaks the job into structure, dormer or roof work, stairs, fire protection and finish. Anything hidden until the roof is opened is shown as a provisional sum. No surprises in a lump total.

Timescales and Build Process for Hedge End Homes

The mess, and where it goes

Most people fear the dust more than the noise. They are right to. The answer is sequence. The roof and dormer are built from outside, on scaffold, while the loft hatch stays sealed. The house below carries on as normal for most of the build.

The day the stairs go in

The staircase is the one stage that comes through the house. The landing is sheeted off, the opening is cut and trimmed, and the stair is fitted in as short a window as the job allows. It is the worst day. It is also one day, not the whole job.

From shell to room

After the stairs come insulation, plasterboard, fire doors and joinery. Our own team covers the carpentry too, from the new floor to the doors, so the fit-out follows the build without a gap. Building control inspects the structure and the fire route before the room is signed off.

Ask Buildings For Life Ltd about Loft Conversions in Hedge End and find out at the survey whether your hip or gable roof gives the headroom a proper room needs.

Quick Quote OnlineCall Now: 07853 945013

Planning Permission and Permitted Development

When no application is needed

Many loft conversions fall under permitted development. The added roof volume must stay within 40 cubic metres on a terraced house and 50 cubic metres on a semi or detached house. Nothing can extend beyond the roof slope facing the road, and materials must look similar to the house.

When it is not that simple

Some Hedge End estates had permitted development rights removed when they were built. Check first. Eastleigh Borough Council can confirm the position, and a lawful development certificate puts it in writing before work starts.

Building Regulations, always

Planning is sometimes optional. Building Regulations are not. Structure, fire escape, stair headroom, insulation and sound between floors all need sign-off.

Benefits and Return on Investment

Space without losing garden

Hedge End has grown faster than any other town in the Borough of Eastleigh over the last twenty years. Plots on newer estates are often compact. The garden stays. Building up keeps it intact. That is the case for a loft over a rear extension.

When a loft is the wrong answer

Headroom decides it. Low roofs sometimes cannot give usable headroom without a full roof rebuild. Then the space is better found at ground level. Whether you need loft conversions in Hedge End or house extensions from our extension builders in Hedge End, the survey shows which one your house suits.

What you are left with

A proper room with a proper stair, built to the rules.

Loft Conversions in Hedge End: Your Questions Answered

Do I need planning permission for a loft conversion in Hedge End?

Often not, if the extra roof volume stays within the permitted development limits and nothing projects from the roof slope facing the road. Some estates had those rights removed when they were built, so check with Eastleigh Borough Council or get a lawful development certificate first.

Will my roof structure take the load?

The existing ceiling joists will not carry a room on their own. New floor joists go in beside them, usually with steel beams bearing on the walls below. A structural engineer sizes them from your house as it is.

Can a Grange Park semi with a hip roof be converted?

Usually, yes. A hip roof gives less headroom than a gable, so the hip is often built up to a gable or a dormer is added at the back. The survey shows which works for your roof and whether it stays within permitted development.

Can we live in our Hedge End house during a loft conversion?

Yes. The roof work is done from scaffold outside while the loft hatch stays sealed. The one disruptive stage is cutting in the staircase, which is sheeted off and kept as short as the job allows.

What fire safety work does a loft conversion need?

Turning a two storey house into three storeys needs a protected escape route: fire doors to the habitable rooms off the stair and a stair that leads down to an exit. Building control checks it before sign-off.
